content.text:
No — the opposite conclusion, and the measurement makes it clear-cut.

All 9 sites already use `*`. **PLR0913 counts keyword-only arguments**, so the three `config_sync` helpers I just fixed still fire it despite now being keyword-only:

```
config_sync.py:167  PLR0913 (7 > 5)   ← has `*`, fixed for PLR0917
config_sync.py:198  PLR0913 (6 > 5)   ← has `*`, fixed for PLR0917
config_sync.py:223  PLR0913 (7 > 5)   ← has `*`, fixed for PLR0917
```

The rest are `_run_sync`, `_async_run_sync`, `sync_config_to_target`, `Orchestrator.__init__`, and a test helper — all already `*`-separated with documented params. They're the same four CLI flags (`auto_accept`, `allow_out_of_order`, `allow_first_sync`, `dry_run`) threaded from argv down to the orchestrator.

So PLR0913 fires on precisely the shape PLR0917 demands you write. The hazard it nominally guards — ambiguity at the call site — is already gone; what's left is raw arity. Satisfying it would mean inventing an options dataclass to appease a counter, on 9 sites with zero defects between them. Different from PLR0917, where 3 of 4 hits were a real transposition risk.

The existing ignore is right. I did tighten its rationale, since "we have complex configs" doesn't explain why the sibling rule stays on:
